one: We have one nose and one mouth.
One is the smallest whole number.
One is a singular pronoun which means someone or people. It is used more often in formal writing.
It is easy to see the difference if one looks closely enough.
online: If a system is online, it is connected (generally electronically) to a larger network.
I do a lot of shopping online, so I almost never have to leave the house.
If a machine is online, it is turned on and is ready to do work.
Since the printer is back online, you should be able to again print from it.
on: positioned at the upper surface of, touching from above
The apple is on the table.
Tim was born on the 4th of July.
Shall we stop for lunch or shall we drive on?
about, dealing with the subject of
I have a book on history.
I have no money on me at the moment.
He was arrested on suspicion of bribery.
If something is on, it is active, functioning or operating.
only: no more than; no other than; just
There are only three schools in this town.
Just one or just a few; this and no other; no more than this.
She is the only woman doctor in this city.
An only child, son, girl, etc. has no brothers or sisters.
You use only to introduce a fact that prevents a statement from being completely true.
They probably could do it, only you never let them try.
ongoing: Something is ongoing if it's continuing to happen without stopping in one long period of time.
The growth of bones is still ongoing at age 12.
once: We go to the house once a year.
at a time in the past, but not now
It was hard to believe that once we had been friends.
onto: He walked along pier and onto the ship.
onshore: He came onshore after five weeks at sea.
onwards: The explorers moved onwards, ever deeper into the jungle.
onlooker: An onlooker is someone who watches but does not participate.
I wasn't in the fight. I was only an onlooker.
onboard: If something is onboard, it has been taken or used on any kind of vehicle or boat.
If something is done onboard, it is done on or in a vehicle or boat; it is done aboard it.
onion: An onion is a vegetable. They can make you cry when you cut them.
She liked eating onions, but they made her cry.
onset: The onset of something is the time when it begins (usually something bad).
onomatopoeia: Onomatopoeia is when a word sounds like a natural sound, such as woof, click, buzz, crackle, bang, boom, moo, crash, shh and squelch.
onanism: Onanism is an act of masturbation.
Onanism is when you ejaculate outside the vagina during sex.
ontology: Ontology is a part of philosophy under the branch of metaphysics which studies the nature of being, becoming, existence and reality.
onomasiology: Onomasiology is the branch of linguistics concerned with "how do you express X?". It gives the words for a given concept. A thesaurus is often used for this job.
oniochalasia: Oniochalasia is when a person buys things to relax themselves.
oncology: Oncology is the study of the development, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of tumors.
oncologist: An oncologist is a doctor or scientist who oncology.
onus: An onus is something that is a person's duty or responsibility.
The onus is on the landlord to make sure the walls are protected from mildew.
onomatopoeic: If something is onomatopoeic, it is related to onomatopoeia.
oneself: Oneself is a word that stands in for words like "myself", "himself", and "herself". It is meant to refer to people in general, nobody in particular.
It's a good idea to check oneself in the mirror before going outside.
oncoming: Oncoming traffic, cars, trains, etc are facing, travelling towards, or moving in the opposite direction to another road-user.
Look carefully before pulling out into oncoming traffic.
An oncoming storm, wave, season, crisis, etc. is one that will arrive soon.
They rushed to prepare for the oncoming storm.
one-quarter: One-quarter is one of four equals parts of a whole.
ontario: Ontario is a province in Canada, its capital is Toronto.
oniony: If something is oniony, it smells or tastes like onion.
onesie: A onesie is a one-piece attire.
oneiric: If something is oneiric, it is related to a person's dreams.
If something is oneiric, it resembles a dream.
